P1.title: Two coffee shops' customers
P1.label: Practice scenario written for this kit from your class materials; the company is made up.
paras: A coffee company surveyed customers at two locations.
table: A place to study with friends

P2.title: FreshFold laundry pods
P2.attr: Practice scenario: a new product and its research.
P2.label: Practice scenario written for this kit from your class materials; the company is made up.
paras: FreshFold wants to sell plant-based laundry pods. It reads a government report on household spending, interviews 12 parents about how they do laundry, and shows two package designs to website visitors to see which one sells more. It also wonders whether it can make pods that dissolve in cold water, since its factory has never made pods before.

questions.stem: Which difference between the shops is psychographic?
options: The most common age of the customers who come into each of the two coffee shops
questions.exp: Reasons and lifestyle are psychographic.

questions.stem: Which shop's typical customer likely has the higher lifetime value per year?
options: Campus, because students will keep coming to the shop for all four years of college

questions.stem: What is the company doing by treating these as two groups?
options: Targeting, because it has picked the downtown customers as the only group it wants to serve
questions.exp: Dividing customers into similar groups is segmentation.
why: It divided; it hasn't chosen yet.

questions.stem: For campus, which promotion fits the data BEST?
options: Faster drive-through lanes for people rushing to work every morning before nine o'clock
questions.exp: Match the message to why the segment buys.

questions.stem: The government report on household spending is:
options: Primary research, because FreshFold is using it to answer a question about its own new product
questions.exp: Existing data is secondary.

questions.stem: Interviewing 12 parents MAINLY gives FreshFold:
options: A reliable percentage of all households that would buy the pods at a given price
questions.exp: Interviews give qualitative why.

questions.stem: Showing two package designs and comparing sales is:
options: A focus group, because FreshFold is learning which design website visitors say they like best
questions.exp: Two versions, real responses.

questions.stem: "Can our factory make pods that dissolve in cold water?" is a question about:
options: Desirability, because customers will want pods that work in cold water to save on energy
questions.exp: Resources, technology and expertise are feasibility.
why: The question is whether FreshFold can make it.

P3.title: Velo e-bikes
P3.label: Practice scenario written for this kit from your class materials; the company is made up.
paras: Velo sells a $2,800 electric bike. Riders can test-ride with a salesperson at weekend events. Velo also posts ads on social media and sponsors a city bike-to-work day that local news covers. In December, it offers $300 off for one week to clear last year's models.

questions.stem: Weekend test rides with a salesperson are:
options: Sales promotion, because the test rides are free and only offered on a few weekends
questions.exp: One-on-one demos for a big purchase.
why: No price incentive; a salesperson demonstrates.

questions.stem: Why does personal selling fit Velo's bike?
options: It's a routine purchase that customers make every week, so they need reminders to buy it
questions.exp: Expensive, complex purchases need detail and demos.

questions.stem: Sponsoring bike-to-work day with news coverage is:
options: Media advertising, because the news broadcast is shown on television to thousands of people
questions.exp: Community events that build goodwill are PR.
why: It's goodwill, not a paid ad.

questions.stem: The one-week $300 discount is MAINLY meant to:
options: Build long-term loyalty with customers who will buy many more bikes from Velo over time
questions.exp: Short-term incentives drive quick decisions or clear stock.

sections.name: Math drills: CAC, markup, margin, CTR, conversion, ROAS
tips: Read the question first, then the scenario, so you know what to look for.
Several choices can be true. Pick the one the scenario supports BEST.
Use the numbers: if a table is given, at least one question needs it.
Watch for choices that are too extreme ("always," "guarantees") or that answer a different question.

questions.stem: A lamp costs $50 and sells for $60. What are its markup and margin?
options: 16.7% markup and 20% margin, because the profit is ten dollars and margin is always larger

questions.stem: A backpack costs $40. The store wants a 50% markup. What should it charge?
options: $80, because a fifty percent markup means doubling the amount that the backpack cost to make

questions.stem: A phone case sells for $25 and costs $15. What is the profit margin?
options: 67%, because the ten dollars of profit should be divided by the fifteen-dollar cost of the case

questions.stem: A business spent $8,000 on online ads and $2,000 on social media, plus $1,500 training new employees. It gained 400 new customers. Using only acquisition costs, what is its CAC?
options: $28.75, because all three of the amounts the business spent should be divided by the new customers
questions.exp: ($8,000 + $2,000) ÷ 400 = $25 (your worksheet has no key: VERIFY).

questions.stem: An ad was shown 80,000 times and clicked 1,200 times. What is its CTR?
options: 15%, because twelve hundred clicks divided by eighty thousand impressions equals fifteen percent

questions.stem: A site had 2,400 visitors and 96 bought. What is the conversion rate?
options: 25%, because twenty-four hundred visitors divided by ninety-six buyers is about twenty-five

questions.stem: A $3,000 campaign brought $12,000 in sales. What is the ROAS?
options: 9, because twelve thousand dollars minus three thousand dollars leaves nine thousand dollars

questions.stem: Ad A cost $2,400 and brought 80 customers. Ad B cost $1,800 and brought 45. Which has the lower CAC?
options: Ad B, because it cost six hundred dollars less to run than Ad A did over the same period

sections.name: Mock test (40 questions)
tips: Read the question first, then the scenario, so you know what to look for.
Several choices can be true. Pick the one the scenario supports BEST.
Use the numbers: if a table is given, at least one question needs it.
Watch for choices that are too extreme ("always," "guarantees") or that answer a different question.

N1.title: Peak Smoothies
N1.attr: Practice scenario: customer data at a smoothie chain.
N1.label: Practice scenario written for this kit from your class materials; the company is made up.
paras: Peak Smoothies runs 12 shops near colleges. Its rewards app records every order. Managers learned that most app users are 18 to 24 and earn under $30,000 a year, and that in interviews they say they choose Peak because they can customize drinks and order ahead between classes. Last quarter Peak spent money to win new customers and launched a points program to keep them.

N2.title: The sneaker drop
N2.attr: Practice scenario: a product page built to persuade.
N2.label: Practice scenario written for this kit from your class materials; the company is made up.
paras: A sneaker brand releases a limited shoe online at 10 a.m. Saturday. The product page shows a counter reading "Only 212 pairs left," a banner saying "Over 40,000 runners already own our shoes," and a quote from a well-known physical therapist praising the shoe's support. Members who signed up for early alerts last year get an email saying, "You told us you'd be first in line. Here's your link."
Many buyers say they decided within minutes. Some later wrote that they were bored at home that morning and "just clicked."

N3.title: BrightBite's research plan
N3.attr: Practice scenario: planning market research for a new snack.
N3.label: Practice scenario written for this kit from your class materials; the company is made up.
paras: BrightBite wants to launch a high-protein chip for teen athletes. Its hypothesis: at least 25% of teen athletes would buy the chip at $3 a bag. The marketing team proposed the steps below. Separately, a database shows the four largest snack brands hold most of the market.
table: Buy an industry report on the size of the protein-snack market
Survey 1,000 high school athletes about price and flavor
Hold 3 focus groups with 8 athletes each
Sell two bag designs on its website and compare purchases
Ask office staff, mostly ages 40 to 60, what flavors teens like

N4.title: TrailCam
N4.attr: Practice scenario: a product over time.
N4.label: Practice scenario written for this kit from your class materials; the company is made up.
paras: TrailCam makes a small, rugged camera for hikers. It tested a hand-built version with 50 hikers in 2019, then launched nationally. The company has used the line "Built for where you go" since its founding. Its 2024 campaign line was "Summer of the Summit."

N5.title: Four ways to price a bike shop
N5.label: Practice scenario written for this kit from your class materials; the company is made up.
paras: Spoke & Gear sells bikes and repairs. The owner is reviewing four items.

N6.title: ColdCase coolers
N6.attr: Practice scenario: pricing power under pressure.
N6.label: Practice scenario written for this kit from your class materials; the company is made up.
paras: ColdCase sells a patented cooler that keeps ice for 10 days. Fans say no other cooler comes close, and sales held steady when ColdCase raised its price from $250 to $300 last year.

This spring, a rival released a nearly identical cooler for $150. At the same time, a heat wave knocked out power across a nearby region, and some ColdCase retailers there raised cooler prices to $750 for a week.

N7.title: Glow Lab skincare
N7.label: Practice scenario written for this kit from your class materials; the company is made up.
paras: Glow Lab sells a skin cream on its own website and wants to grow fast. The table compares two options. Glow Lab is also developing a stronger cream with a prescription-strength ingredient.
table: Sell through a national drugstore chain
Build national shipping and customer service

N8.title: FitFuel's launch campaign
N8.attr: Practice scenario: measuring a promotion campaign.
N8.label: Practice scenario written for this kit from your class materials; the company is made up.
paras: FitFuel launched a meal-prep delivery service with several promotion tools at once. It tracked each channel for one month.
table: Emails to past customers with a 20% code

questions.stem: Which piece of Peak's information is psychographic?
options: Most app users are between eighteen and twenty-four years old and earn under $30,000
questions.exp: Values and preferences explain why people buy.

questions.stem: Based on the table, what was Peak's customer acquisition cost?
options: $28.33, because all three of the costs in the table should be divided by the 600 new customers

questions.stem: What do the spending figures BEST suggest about the points program?
options: It lowers acquisition cost, because rewards members spend almost three times as much per year
questions.exp: Members spend $420 a year vs. $150: higher lifetime value.
why: Spending more per year raises CLV.

questions.stem: Which is the BEST target customer for Peak's next ad?
options: Retirees who live far from campus, since they have the most free time to visit the smoothie shops
College students who order between classes
questions.exp: Target the buyers most likely to purchase.

questions.stem: Peak's app stores card numbers. Which practice would MOST reduce its biggest data risk?
options: Collecting even more personal data from each customer so that its rewards can be more personal
questions.exp: Poor security leads to breaches, fraud and identity theft.

questions.stem: "Only 212 pairs left" uses which principle?
options: Consensus, because it tells shoppers how many other runners have already bought the shoe
questions.exp: Limited supply raises perceived value.

questions.stem: The physical therapist's quote uses which principle?
options: Liking, because shoppers are likely to feel positively toward a friendly health professional
questions.exp: Trust in experts is authority.

questions.stem: The email "You told us you'd be first in line" MOST directly uses:
options: Reciprocity, because the brand is giving members a special link before everyone else gets one
questions.exp: Reminding people of past commitments triggers consistency.
why: It leans on their past commitment.

questions.stem: "I was bored at home that morning and just clicked" describes which factor?
options: Personal, because the buyer's age and income decide whether a shopper can afford the shoes
questions.exp: Mood and timing are situational factors.

questions.stem: Buyers deciding within minutes BEST shows:
options: Habit buying, because many of these buyers have purchased shoes from this brand in the past
questions.exp: On-the-spot decisions are impulsive.

questions.stem: Step 1 (the industry report) is an example of:
options: Primary research, because BrightBite will use the report's numbers to make its own decisions
questions.exp: Existing data from reports is secondary.

questions.stem: Which step BEST tests the hypothesis about paying $3?
options: Step 3, because focus groups let athletes explain in depth why they would pay three dollars
questions.exp: A large survey gives a percentage to compare with 25%.

questions.stem: What does Step 4 add that the survey can't?
options: The reasons why athletes prefer one bag design over the other, explained in their own words
questions.exp: An A/B test measures real behavior.

questions.stem: What is the BIGGEST problem with Step 5?
options: The questions are leading, because staff will be asked which flavors they personally love the most
The sample doesn't represent teen athletes
questions.exp: Ask the people you're studying.
why: The issue is who is asked.

questions.stem: Which chart BEST shows the four largest brands' share of the snack market?
options: A line graph, because each brand's share of the market has been changing year after year
questions.exp: Pie charts show parts of a whole.
why: The question is the current split.

questions.stem: Based on the table, which stage was TrailCam in during 2021–2022?
options: Maturity, because by 2022 the company was selling ninety thousand cameras every single year
questions.exp: Accelerating sales and new rivals mark growth.

questions.stem: Which stage BEST describes 2023–2024?
options: Decline, because TrailCam sold about one thousand fewer cameras in 2024 than it did in 2023
questions.exp: Sales leveling off with many rivals is maturity.
why: A tiny dip with flat sales is maturity.

questions.stem: Which move fits TrailCam's current stage BEST?
options: Spend most of the budget on awareness ads, since many hikers still haven't heard of the camera
Add features and reward loyal buyers
questions.exp: In maturity, defend share with differentiation, loyalty and innovation.

questions.stem: The 2019 test with 50 hikers was MAINLY used to:
options: Build awareness among millions of hikers through news stories about the new camera
questions.exp: Testing with real users before launch is validation.

questions.stem: "Built for where you go" (used since founding) is TrailCam's:
options: Slogan, because it is a short and catchy line that appears on many of TrailCam's ads
questions.exp: Long-term, whole-brand lines are taglines; "Summer of the Summit" is a slogan.

questions.stem: What is the markup on the basic helmet?
options: 20%, because the five dollars of profit is divided by the twenty-five-dollar selling price

questions.stem: Which item has the HIGHEST profit margin?
options: The tune-up, because the shop earns fifteen dollars on every tune-up and needs almost no parts

questions.stem: The package priced at $349 instead of $389 is BEST described as:
options: A loss leader, because the shop is losing money on the lights in order to sell the bike
questions.exp: Several items together for less than separately.
why: It's still profitable; items sold together for less.

questions.stem: The custom carbon bike's $4,000 price for a $2,400 cost MOST likely reflects:
options: Cost-based pricing, because the shop first had to find out how much the custom bike cost
questions.exp: Unique, high-quality items suit value-based pricing.
why: Price reflects what riders think it's worth.

questions.stem: If the owner priced the helmet at $18, what would happen?
options: Each helmet would earn two dollars more, because a lower price attracts more customers
questions.exp: A price below per-unit cost brings no profit.

questions.stem: Last year's price rise with steady sales suggests ColdCase's demand was:
options: Elastic, because ColdCase's customers clearly noticed that the price had gone up by fifty dollars
questions.exp: Little change in buying after a price rise means inelastic demand.

questions.stem: Why did ColdCase have high pricing power last year?
options: Because coolers are a necessity that every household must buy at least once each summer
It had a unique, patented product
questions.exp: Unique products with no close substitutes have more pricing power.

questions.stem: What will the rival's $150 cooler MOST likely do?
options: Make ColdCase's demand even less elastic, since fans will see the cheap rival as lower quality
questions.exp: A cheaper, nearly identical substitute weakens pricing power.

questions.stem: The retailers charging $750 during the power outage is MOST likely:
options: Dynamic pricing, because prices normally rise when demand goes up during busy times of the year
questions.exp: Sharp increases during emergencies can be illegal gouging.

questions.stem: If ColdCase and the rival secretly agreed to both charge $300, that would be:
options: Competitive pricing, because each company is setting its price based on what the other charges
questions.exp: Agreeing on prices instead of competing is illegal collusion.

questions.stem: Selling through the drugstore chain would make Glow Lab's channel:
options: Direct, because customers would still be buying Glow Lab's own cream in the drugstores
questions.exp: Selling through an intermediary is indirect.
why: The question is the channel type.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes the drugstore option's trade-off?
options: More control over price, but fewer stores, because the drugstore limits where the cream is sold
More reach, less money and control
questions.exp: Indirect: reach vs. money per unit and control.

questions.stem: If Glow Lab stays direct and grows nationally, what is its biggest challenge?
options: Losing control over how its cream is priced and displayed to customers in the stores
questions.exp: Direct channels need their own logistics and service.

questions.stem: The prescription-strength cream MOST likely must be sold:
options: Only on Glow Lab's website, since online sales give the company the most control over the price
questions.exp: Some products must use specific channels for health and safety.

questions.stem: Which plan would BEST balance reach and control for the current cream?
options: Close the website and sell only in drugstores, because four thousand stores reach more people
Keep the website and add the drugstore
questions.exp: Many firms mix channels to balance reach, cost and control.
why: Gives up all control and data.

questions.stem: What was the social ads' click-through rate?
options: 0.1%, because the four hundred orders are divided by the four hundred thousand impressions
why: That's orders ÷ impressions; CTR uses clicks.

questions.stem: Of the people who clicked the emails, what percentage ordered?
options: 1.2%, because two hundred forty orders are divided by the twenty thousand emails that were sent
why: That's orders ÷ impressions; the question asks about people who clicked.

questions.stem: Which tool had the HIGHEST return on ad spend?
options: The TV spot, because it reached one million viewers, more than any other tool in the campaign

questions.stem: The emails with a 20% code are BEST classified as:
options: Public relations, because the emails help FitFuel build goodwill with its past customers
Direct marketing and a sales promotion
questions.exp: Tools overlap: a targeted email with a coupon is both.

questions.stem: Based on the data, what is the BEST next step for FitFuel?
options: Spend more on TV, because television reached the largest number of people during the month
Shift some TV money to email and social
questions.exp: Digital tools here are measurable and earn more per dollar.
why: TV earned the least per dollar.

examTips: Built like your Unit 1 test: 40 multiple-choice questions, one scenario per page, 5 questions each. Your Unit 2 test format isn't known yet.
Turn the Timer on and leave Shuffle off. About one minute per question.
Many questions have two good answers: choose the one the scenario supports best.
